findings.title: Equal-priority providers can silently select a non-FIPS implementation
findings.body: `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider` all return order 200, so sorting does not define which one wins when more than one is available. The first provider in ServiceLoader discovery order is silently selected; a deployment containing both FIPS and the default provider can therefore run with the default implementation instead of FIPS, whereas the previous behavior rejected multiple providers. Assign distinct priorities or reject ties.

findings.title: Adding an abstract method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: Existing third-party `CryptoProvider` implementations compiled against the previous interface have no `order()` implementation. `CryptoIntegration` now invokes `order()` on every discovered provider while sorting, which causes `AbstractMethodError` and prevents crypto initialization for those applications. Make the method backward-compatible with a default implementation or otherwise preserve compatibility.

findings.title: The Bouncy Castle getter returns the default keystore provider
findings.body: This returns the provider that implements the JVM's default keystore type, not a Bouncy Castle provider. Callers using `getBouncyCastleProvider()` for provider-specific algorithms or services will receive the wrong provider and may fail to obtain those services, despite the method contract promising Bouncy Castle.
